summary.text: Feldspars are a group of rock-forming aluminium tectosilicate minerals that also contain cations such as sodium, calcium, potassium or barium.
They make up about 60% of Earth's crust by weight and turn up in igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks.
When feldspars weather chemically they break down by hydrolysis into clay minerals, which is why clays are such abundant weathering products.

facts.label: Weathering products
facts.value: Clays such as illite, smectite and kaolinite

items.prompt: Over centuries, feldspar in a rock reacts with water and breaks down. What common material does this mainly produce?
items.explain: Chemical weathering of feldspar happens by hydrolysis and produces clay minerals, which is why clays are so abundant.

items.prompt: A body of magma is cooling and its first feldspar crystals are forming. What element are they most likely rich in?
items.explain: Calcium-rich plagioclase crystallizes first; it grows more sodium-rich later, and potassium feldspar comes last.

items.prompt: Two identical feldspar grains sit in water, one in neutral water and one in acidic water. Which weathers faster?

options.label: Both weather at the same speed

items.explain: Feldspar dissolves best in acidic or basic solutions, and its weathering speed is set by how fast it dissolves.

items.prompt: How can ions of sodium, potassium or calcium sit inside a feldspar crystal?

options.label: They are dissolved in trapped water
They take the place of oxygen
They coat the outside of each grain
The tetrahedral network has room for them

items.explain: Feldspar's three-dimensional network of tetrahedra is open enough for these cations to fit inside and balance the charge.

items.prompt: Roughly how much of Earth's crust, by weight, is feldspar?
items.explain: Feldspars make up about 60% of the crust by weight.

items.prompt: Geologists classify an igneous rock using the ratio of alkali to plagioclase feldspar together with the proportion of which other mineral?
items.explain: The QAPF classification of igneous rock rests on the two feldspar types plus the proportion of quartz.
